clusters.name: Surfactant-mediated solubilization and emulsification
clusters.description: Amphiphilic agents solubilize oils and waxes into micelles or emulsions, reducing adhesion and enabling removal with minimal water.

clusters.name: Enzymatic or microbial digestion
clusters.description: Enzymes or microbes selectively break down organic soils and odors into soluble fragments for easier extraction.

clusters.name: Reactive-oxidant generation (catalytic/plasma/electrochemical)
clusters.description: Produce reactive species in situ (oxidants, radicals) to chemically decompose organic stains and microbes without bulk water.

clusters.name: Phase-change solvent cycling (evaporation/condensation/pressurization)
clusters.description: Use controlled vaporization and recondensation or pressure swings to dissolve, mobilize, and recover contaminants with little liquid.

clusters.name: Supercritical / near‑critical fluid solvation
clusters.description: Use supercritical fluids to dissolve and extract organic contaminants with minimal or no conventional liquid water.

clusters.name: Micro-volume solvent application
clusters.description: Deliver very small droplets or thin films to activate chemistry at stain sites without saturating textiles.

clusters.name: Controlled minimal-liquid exposure chamber
clusters.description: Confine garments in a sealed environment maintaining high humidity or minimal liquid volume for targeted cleaning.

clusters.name: Continuous purification and recirculation
clusters.description: Separate contaminants from transport fluid (filtering, trapping) and return cleaned solvent/water for immediate reuse.

clusters.name: Sorbent-based adsorption and regeneration
clusters.description: Use engineered adsorbents to capture soils, then regenerate (heat/vacuum/pressure) to remove and reuse the sorbent and fluid.

clusters.name: Microencapsulated agent release
clusters.description: Store cleaning actives in microcapsules that rupture on trigger, releasing concentrated actives locally to minimize water.

clusters.name: Sacrificial peelable coating removal
clusters.description: Apply a removable film that binds contaminants, solidifies, and is peeled off carrying soils away from fabric.

clusters.name: Foam and bubble-mediated lift and flotation
clusters.description: Use foamed media or bubbles to attach to hydrophobic particles and lift them away from fibers for collection.

clusters.name: Solid-contact mechanical abrasion
clusters.description: Use discrete solids, pads, or textured media to physically abrade or transfer soils from fibers, then remove the media.

clusters.name: Rotational and tumbling mechanical agitation
clusters.description: Create relative motion and collisions to mechanically dislodge soils and reorient fabric surfaces for easier extraction.

clusters.name: Vibrational and pulsed-air agitation
clusters.description: Apply ultrasound, surface acoustic waves, or rapid air pulses to loosen particles and break adhesive bonds without excess liquid.

clusters.name: Field-driven transport and capture
clusters.description: Use electric, ionic, or magnetic fields to move charged/magnetic particles or induce electrostatic capture for later removal.

clusters.name: Electrowetting and surface-actuated wetting control
clusters.description: Use electrical control of local wetting to move, merge, or shed microdroplets and mobilize soils from fabric surfaces.

clusters.name: Vacuum and pneumatic suction removal
clusters.description: Generate negative pressure to lift, entrain, and transport loosened particulates and gases away from textiles.

clusters.name: Pressure- and flow-induced pore flushing
clusters.description: Force fluid through fabric pore networks to flush entrained contaminants from within fiber bundles.

clusters.name: Gentle continuous extraction flow
clusters.description: Maintain a low-velocity background flow to capture suspended particles and dissolved residues without disrupting fabrics.

clusters.name: Thermal and crystallization-induced stress cycling
clusters.description: Use freeze/thaw, salt crystallization, or local heating/cooling to create mechanical stresses that pry out embedded dirt.

clusters.name: Localized electromagnetic heating of contaminants
clusters.description: Use targeted IR, microwave, or RF to preferentially heat soils, loosen adhesion, or volatilize residues while sparing fabric.

clusters.name: Shockwave and impulse detachment
clusters.description: Produce rapid pressure transients to fracture soil–fiber bonds and eject contaminants for collection.

clusters.name: Adsorptive chelation and complexation
clusters.description: Use chelating agents or complex-formers to sequester metal-bound or hydrophobic contaminants into removable complexes.

clusters.name: Stimulus-responsive surface release
clusters.description: Temporarily change surface adhesion (chemical or physical trigger) to actively release bound contaminants for capture.

clusters.name: Electrocoagulation and electroaggregation
clusters.description: Use electrical currents to destabilize colloids and aggregate fine contaminants for easier filtration and removal.

clusters.name: Field-modulated fluid rheology
clusters.description: Change fluid viscosity or viscoelastic properties via fields or additives to mechanically stress and release adhered particles.

clusters.name: Targeted sensing and localized dosing
clusters.description: Detect stains or soil concentration and apply localized cleaning (spray, heat, mechanical) to minimize total water use.
